He points to a diagram depicting a simple circuit with a bulb, battery, switch, and wire. The corresponding symbols of the items are circled, indicating that the circuit is composed of these components. The segment transitions back to the boy, looking more contemplative now. A similar diagram appears in the background, but this time, the positive and negative terminals of the battery are emphasized, with corresponding symbols. The boy identifies this as the positive and negative terminal of a battery. The man returns, affirming the boy's correct understanding. He explains that any appliance run on electricity will have an electrical circuit. The scene then transitions back to the boy on the green lawn, where he looks to be pondering what he was just told.
